item.title: Brazil's Central Bank sells US$1 billion to curb the dollar's rise

The move brought initial relief, but the dollar rose again in the afternoon.

item.title: Colombia to euthanise hippos for the first time: ten animals in four months
item.description: Colombia's government will for the first time carry out chemical euthanasia on hippopotamuses, an invasive species in the country since drug lord Pablo Escobar brought the first animals to his estate in the 1980s. The Environment Ministry announced on Wednesday that ten animals in Antioquia department, located near populated areas, will be put down over the next four months.

item.title: Ueno Bank collapse claims Paraguay’s attorney general and the head of Itaipú
item.description: Paraguay’s Attorney General Emiliano Rolón resigned on Tuesday in the face of imminent impeachment, and the Paraguayan director of the binational Itaipú dam, Justo Zacarías Irún, was dismissed on Wednesday, in the latest wave of departures triggered by the collapse of Ueno Bank. At least a dozen senior officials have left their posts since the bank was taken over on November 3, among them President Santiago Peña, who was removed from office and is in prison.

item.description:

item.title: Hegseth uses Venezuela visit to boast of Maduro’s capture by US military
item.description:
Defense secretary asserts US dominance on trip that would have seemed ‘impossible, almost unbelievable’ a year ago

Pete Hegseth has used his first visit to Venezuela since US special forces abducted its former president, Nicolás Maduro, to boast of the dictator’s capture during what he called “the single most sophisticated military operation in the history of Latin America”.

Maduro was controversially seized by Delta Force operatives in the early hours of 3 January, setting in motion an improbable rapprochement between Washington and Venezuela’s anti-imperialist “Chavista” regime, which has ruled since 1999.

item.title: US Democrats nominate Jeffries to be first Black House speaker
item.description: Hakeem Jeffries is on the cusp of becoming the first Black speaker of the US House of Representatives after Democrats elected him their leader Wednesday following a sweeping midterm election triumph. Jeffries faced no declared challenger, although opposition from some newly elected progressives had exposed divisions over how Democrats should wield their newfound power. FRANCE 24's Fraser Jackson reports from Washington.

item.title: The Quechua rapper and an artistic movement reclaiming language of the Incas
item.description:
Renata Flores has gained global recognition for her music in Indigenous language whose speakers have faced social stigma

With her long black hair braided into beaded plaits, a delicate silver nose ring, and intricately patterned Andean textile draped around her chest above baggy, low-riding jeans, Renata Flores is a visual reflection of her music: a fusion of traditional and transgressive, old and new, rural and urban.

Nicknamed the “queen of Quechua rap”, Flores, 25, has earned global recognition for mixing Peru’s main Indigenous language and Andean instruments with the urban beats of trap, rap, hip-hop and reggaeton.

item.title: Isolated Brazilian tribe emerges amid alarm over threats to group’s way of life
item.description:
Indigenous Awá people of Amazon make contact with villagers and accept food to take back to territory

About 20 Indigenous people emerged from isolation in Brazil’s Amazon rainforest, several organizations reported on Tuesday, raising the alarm about increased invasions into the tribe’s territory.

According to the NGO Survival International, members of the Awá people, who live in voluntary isolation, arrived on Monday in a village and made contact with a government team in a “historic encounter”.

item.title: Costa Rican journalist shot dead in first such killing in 25 years
item.description:
Camilo Rodriguez’s death comes as the country grapples with a surge in drug violence

The Costa Rican journalist Camilo Rodríguez, who gained prominence for publishing allegations against ⁠suspected drug traffickers and politicians, was shot dead on Monday, authorities said.

The first known killing of a journalist ⁠in Costa Rica in ⁠25 years, ​Rodriguez’s death comes as the country grapples with a surge in drug violence driven by international trafficking groups, despite long ⁠being regarded as one of Central America’s most peaceful and stable democracies.
